solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gardener's skill?

parts.note: the famous eighteenth-century landscape gardener Lancelot Brown carried a nickname that also means ability

explanation.surface: A question about what talent a gardener has.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown was the great English landscape gardener, so his nickname doubles as a word for skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A skill is an ability or competence, which is what the word names in everyday use.

clue.text: Island reporter covers America

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of, and so covers, the next

parts.note: a cub is a young, inexperienced newspaper reporter

explanation.surface: A journalist is assigned to report on the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' looks like a journalist's beat, but in a down answer it means CUB sits above A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean nation is a large island south of Florida.

clue.text: Peg about to make sharper radio show

indicators.note: the peg goes round, about, the other piece

parts.note: a peg is a pin used to fasten things
to hone is to sharpen a blade

explanation.surface: Someone sharpens a peg for a radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme in which listeners call the studio by telephone is a type of radio show.

clue.text: One who has committed a grave offence

definitions.text: One who has committed a grave offence

parts.words: One who has committed a grave offence
parts.note: a grave offence sounds like a serious crime, but here it is literally an offence involving a grave: digging up corpses

explanation.surface: A description of a serious criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: Grave means serious on the surface; read literally it is a burial plot, robbed by those who stole corpses for anatomists.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpse thieves dug up freshly buried bodies, a crime literally committed at a grave.

clue.text: Stable — but it could fall off the back of a lorry

definitions.meaning: a stall in a stable where a horse can move freely

definitions.text: it could fall off the back of a lorry
definitions.meaning: a crate not tied down is liable to slide off a truck; 'fallen off the back of a lorry' is British slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A horse box, unless it is insecure cargo on a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A large stall where a horse is left untied is a horse compartment in a stable; and an unsecured crate could literally tumble from a truck.

clue.text: Pedlar or potter?

definitions.meaning: a travelling mender and seller of pots and pans
to fiddle aimlessly with something, as a verb

explanation.surface: Asking whether a travelling seller also makes pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like a maker of pots; here it is the verb meaning to fiddle about.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinker was an itinerant seller and mender, and to tinker is to potter about fiddling with things.

clue.text: Injure limb after start of holiday

indicators.note: the limb comes after the opening letter
the first letter of the word holiday is taken

parts.note: an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: Someone hurts an arm right at the beginning of a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To harm someone is to hurt or injure them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Not many reformed — plenty will make an example here

definitions.text: plenty will make an example here

indicators.note: formed again, so the letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Few people have mended their ways, but there is plenty to learn from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not many' is itself a word of opposite meaning to 'plenty', so the clue words are an example of what the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: A word opposite in meaning, such as few against plenty, is what the grammatical term names.

clue.text: One revels in tight score, getting runs

parts.note: tight and merry both mean tipsy
to score a goal is to make one
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A partygoer celebrates a narrow scoring win with runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' suggests a close game, but it means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A reveller is someone who joins in festivity and fun.

clue.text: Noble descent takes precedence in medical analysis

indicators.note: the descent piece goes in front of the noble

parts.note: blood means lineage or descent
a count is a nobleman

explanation.surface: Aristocratic lineage comes first in some medical test.
explanation.definitionFit: A tally of the cells in a sample from the veins is a common laboratory test.

clue.text: One way to make the food go round

definitions.text: One way to make the food go round

parts.words: One way to make the food go round
parts.note: suggests sharing out rations, but means moving a spoon round a pan

explanation.surface: How to share food so everyone has enough.
explanation.walkthrough: Making food 'go round' suggests eking it out; literally it is moving a spoon round the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixing with a spoon in circles literally moves the food round the pan.

clue.text: Becoming suspicious of ratings all mutinying around me

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the small word
the sailors rebel, so their letters break ranks

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An officer grows suspicious as sailors mutiny around him.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratings are ordinary sailors, which suits the mutiny picture; 'mutinying' gives SLLINGARAT, and 'around' wraps that round the officer's own word.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense that something is wrong is the meaning of this idiom.

clue.text: This person gets seconds in dining room

parts.note: the speaker refers to himself as me
s is the abbreviation for second, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone takes a second helping in the dining hall.
explanation.definitionFit: In the armed forces, the room where personnel eat together is so called.

clue.text: Sporting contest cut short means 50-50

indicators.note: the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: an event is a sporting contest
means as in financial means

explanation.surface: A match that ends early leaves things evenly balanced.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting odds of one to one give an equal chance either way.

clue.text: One having a turn on the pitch

definitions.text: One having a turn on the pitch

parts.words: One having a turn on the pitch
parts.note: suggests a player taking a go, but means one who makes a cricket ball turn off the pitch

explanation.surface: A player takes a turn on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a slow bowler makes the ball turn sideways when it bounces on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer whose deliveries deviate after bouncing is the kind of bowler named.

clue.text: Write name above building in America

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tag is a label or name
on, as in resting on top of

explanation.surface: Someone inscribes a name above an American building.
explanation.definitionFit: The US Department of Defense headquarters is a famous building in Virginia.

clue.text: Manual rewritten by former female student

indicators.note: the letters of the word are written again in a different order

explanation.surface: A handbook revised by a woman graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman graduate of a school or university is the feminine Latin term.

clue.text: The continental coin having risen first 100-fold

indicators.note: coin and risen come before the French article

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
risen means up
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A European coin's value has rocketed a hundredfold.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiplied by a hundred is the meaning of this rare adjective.

clue.text: Beginner needs to get a grip?

parts.note: one who needs to get something has none of it
a vice is a gripping tool on a workbench

explanation.surface: A learner must get a better grip.
explanation.walkthrough: One who still needs to get a grip has none, a gripping tool being a vice.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer or learner is a novice.

clue.text: Issuing a refusal to not give freely

indicators.note: loosely, without fixed order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Declining to hand things out generously.
explanation.definitionFit: Using a power of rejection is to block or forbid formally.

clue.text: Sappers apt to be trustworthy

parts.note: RE, Royal Engineers, the British Army's sappers
apt to do something means liable to

explanation.surface: Army engineers are likely to be dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Dependable and trustworthy are synonyms.

clue.text: Graduate's last letter: 'Nothing's fine' — found with a deadly weapon

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts
Z ends the alphabet
zero, shaped like O
okay means fine

explanation.surface: A graduate's final letter says all is well, though found with a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable anti-tank rocket launcher is a lethal weapon.

clue.text: Boring nonsense that may bring the house down?

definitions.text: that may bring the house down?

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: Dull rubbish that might bring the house down with laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring the house down' suggests a hit show; here it is fungal decay that collapses timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Fungal decay of timber weakens a building's structure until it collapses.

clue.text: Going at a moderate pace one after another

definitions.meaning: moving at a horse's gait between walk and canter

explanation.surface: Moving steadily, in succession.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means trotting along, and in British usage also successively without a break.

clue.text: Go round wizard home in Mediterranean island

indicators.note: the first word goes round the second

parts.note: taken as written
Oz is the home of the Wizard in the famous story

explanation.surface: Travel round the wizard's land on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta's sister island is in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Picture cards

definitions.meaning: a children's card game played by matching cards

explanation.surface: Photographs of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot photograph, and also a simple matching card game.

clue.text: The Parisian female at home, stretched out

parts.note: la is the feminine French for the
in means at home

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman is lying at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The past participle of lie means having reclined, stretched out.

clue.text: Uncommon part of speech following a capital start

definitions.text: Uncommon part of speech following a capital start

parts.words: Uncommon part of speech following a capital start
parts.note: a noun that is not a common noun, written with a capital first letter

explanation.surface: A rare word type that begins in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncommon' means rare on the surface, but here it means not a common noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Names of particular people or places are written with initial capitals and contrast with common nouns.

clue.text: Not wholly courageous during storm

indicators.note: only part of the word is used, the inner run of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone is less than brave during a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm is to rant furiously, which is to be in a fury.

clue.text: Light malt Peter's brewed

indicators.note: a brewer mixes malt, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Peter's malt beer is brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: A street lamp is a light on a post along a road.
